title: introduce-inference-cost-gardener-default-curator
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: Customers frequently accept our defaults but still overprovision or underutilize cache/batch settings. This PR introduces the 'Cost Gardener' and a Default Curator that cultivates tenant-specific starter profiles for batching, KV-prefill, and quantization bands. The goal is to reduce first-touch unit cost while keeping latency SLO regressions <= 5% and providing a safe hedge policy for fallbacks.

What this PR does (high level): 1) Adds gardener service (redwood/econ/gardener) that synthesizes per-tenant default bundles from historical sampling and lightweight local-sim-mode. 2) Default Curator CLI (redwood/cli/cost-garden) that can produce: seed-batch-presets, cache-prefix-presets, and rounded quantization bands with safety thresholds. 3) Implements a small policy engine for automated rollback/hedge (tenant-level policy: prefer latency-safety over token-cost when delta > threshold). 4) Telemetry hooks and new metrics: cost_gardener.score, gardener.seed_count, gardener.rollback_trigger. 5) Docs and a guided quickstart: ops can run the curator in dry-run to preview expected unit-econ impact.

Checklist: - [x] Core algorithm + API - [x] CLI and dry-run mode - [x] Telemetry + dashboards (basic) - [x] Unit tests and integration smoke - [x] Docs and examples

Why different: instead of one-size defaults this system emits conservative per-tenant 'seed profiles' based on a compact fingerprint and growth heuristics (garden bed model). The approach prioritizes explainability (why a seed was chosen) and a safety-first rollback policy.

Backward compatibility: defaults are additive; existing default config remains unless an operator applies a curated seed. The gardener only annotates profiles and never forces live rollout without opt-in or configured automatic rollout window.

release_notes: Introduce Cost Gardener and Default Curator: per-tenant seed profiles for batching, cache and quantization defaults; CLI dry-run; telemetry; safety-first rollback policy. Operators should run in dry-run before enabling auto-rollout.
testing: unit: gardener_test covers sampler, simulator interface and policy gating
integration: smoke test runs a small tenant trace in dry-run and asserts no live rollouts
e2e: manual validation documented in operators quickstart
notes_for_launch: Add curated dashboard to staging org, run curator against 3 representative tenants in staging, review metrics for 48h, then opt-in limited auto-rollout
safety_considerations: Automatic rollouts default to off. Hedge policy prioritizes latency SLO. Quant bands are capped to conservative levels in the initial release to avoid regressions.
estimated_impact: Internal estimates: 6-12% median token-cost reduction for eligible tenants in dry-run; tail latency regression expected <3% with current conservative caps
